newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli air raid kills two Lebanese civilians.
newsitem.headline: Israeli air raid kills two Lebanese civilians.

text.p: Israeli warplanes on Tuesday blasted suspected Hizbollah targets in Lebanon's eastern Bekaa Valley, killing two Lebanese civilians and wounding four, security sources said.
The 48th air assault into Lebanon in 1997 came shortly after the pro-Iranian guerrillas attacked a pro-Israeli outpost in Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.

The sources identified the dead as 70-year-old Mohammed Hassan Mozahem and 72-year-old Ali Moussa Akl. This raised to 10 the number of Lebanese civilians killed in Israeli attacks in south Lebanon since the beginning of the year.
Two farmers and two children were also wounded in the attack, the sources added.
Four planes fired a total of eight rockets into the hills of Libbaya-Yohmour in the southeastern part of the Bekaa, north of Israel's occupation zone, the Lebanese sources said.
An Israeli army spokesman confirmed the attack.

"Israel Air Force attack planes struck at Hizbollah targets this morning north of the eastern sector of the security zone in Lebanon. The pilots reported very good hits. All planes returned safely to base."
In a separate incident, a roadside bomb explosion claimed the life of another civilian, Ziad Jehjah, in Jizzine -- a strip of land officially outside the occupation zone but under Israeli control.
No group claimed responsibility for the attack.

Earlier, Hizbollah guerrillas fired mortar bombs into the South Lebanon Army outpost of Ahmadiyyeh inside the zone facing the hills, lightly wounding a pro-Israeli militiaman, according to SLA and Israeli military sources.
On Monday, Israeli commandos in helicopters backed by planes raided suspected Hizbollah targets in southern Lebanon, triggering fierce clashes at Kfour in Nabatiyeh outside the zone.
Five Hizbollah guerrillas were killed later by three roadside bombs planted by Israeli commandos. Five civilians were wounded in the bombings.

Lebanon, which complained about Monday's attack to a five-nation committee monitoring a ceasefire understanding in Lebanon, filed a fresh complaint after the air attacks, foreign ministry sources said.

In April 1996, Israel launched a 17-day blitz on the country, killing about 200 people -- mostly civilians. A U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding banned both Hizbollah and Israeli troops from firing from or at civilian targets.
Hizbollah is fighting Israeli troops and their local militia allies in a bid to oust them from the 15-km (nine-mile) wide south Lebanon occupation zone.
